titel: 449. The psychology of your shadow self

faehigkeiten.grund: Dynamik weder belegt noch ausgeschlossen (Abruf laeuft ueber den Werbedienst podtrac.com) - zu wenig fuer ein Urteil, aber nicht nichts

einzeiler: Exploring the psychology of the shadow self, Karl Jung's theories, and shadow work.
kurzfassung: This episode explores the concept of the shadow self, originating from Karl Jung's analytical psychology. It breaks down how repressed traits, archetypes, and the persona shape our unconscious behavior and self-sabotage. Finally, it discusses practical approaches to encountering and integrating the shadow safely without falling into excessive self-criticism.
stichpunkte: Shadow work focuses on the shadow self and how repressed traits influence behavior unconsciously.
Karl Jung developed analytical psychology and introduced archetypes, the persona, and the shadow.
Freud and Jung disagreed because Freud focused heavily on sexual and aggressive impulses, while Jung emphasized symbols, myths, and the collective unconscious.
Archetypes like the caregiver, hero, and jester have both light and shadow expressions when overidentified with.
The personal shadow develops in childhood when organic reactions are suppressed for acceptance.
Shadow work reveals itself through psychological projection and repeated negative behavior patterns.
Integrating the shadow means bringing unconscious traits into awareness with compassion rather than elimination.
Excessive self-interrogation can become harmful, and working with a psychotherapist provides a safer framework.

kapitel.titel: Karl Jung, Freud, and the Collective Unconscious
When Shadow Work Goes Too Far

clips.hook: The appeal and hidden dangers of uncovering your deep truths
clips.text: A listener calls in to seek advice about losing that special feeling of being chosen after getting engaged to her partner.

clips.hook: How the caregiver archetype turns into codependency
clips.text: Carl Jung's psychological framework divides human nature into distinct components of the unconscious mind.

clips.hook: Energy cannot be destroyed, only converted
clips.text: The shadow represents the hidden aspects of human personality that do not align with societal expectations and norms.

clips.hook: Why shadow work requires looking directly into your worst fears
clips.text: Unconscious patterns often lead people to repeatedly choose romantic partners who are emotionally unavailable and bad for them.

clips.hook: The ultimate goal of shadow work isn't elimination, but understanding
clips.text: Strong emotional reactions like hatred or jealousy toward other people often reveal hidden traits within one's own shadow.

beschreibung:
What is the shadow self? And how do we meet ours? In today's episode we explore what it means to get curious about the shadow parts of ourselves. We take a grounded look at shadow work - where the idea came from, the layers of our psyche, and how the repressed parts of ourselves show up.
We explore:
• What Jung meant by the shadow and the persona
• How the dark or disowned parts of ourselves can develop
• Why anger, neediness, ambition, or confidence can feel uncomfortable to acknowledge
• The role of projection, triggers and repeated patterns
• How to approach shadow work cautiously and with curiosity
